events.description: As many as 215 Soviet transports (AN-22s, AN-12s, IL-76s) arrived in Afghanistan from the USSR.
SCC meeting 9:30-10:30 a.m. on Soviet moves in Afghanistan; CIA briefing and decisions on public posture, briefing allies and Congress, no further demarche by the President.
PRC planned for the next day to discuss regional impact of events in Iran and Afghanistan and develop options including UN recourse; CIA to submit covert action status report.
Up to 215 Soviet transport aircraft (AN-22, AN-12, IL-76) arrived in Afghanistan; no ground forces crossed the border at Termez or Kushka.
SCC meeting 9:30-10:30 a.m. on Soviet moves in Afghanistan; decisions on public posture, briefing allies, and Watson demarche.
CIA briefed SCC on Soviet military actions over the past two days.
State to brief Congressional leadership; regional countries to be briefed; Tom Watson to press Soviets for explanation of troop movements.

key_claims: As many as 215 Soviet transports landed in Afghanistan on 25 December 1979, with Kabul airport a major reception point.
No Soviet ground forces at Termez or Kushka had yet crossed into Afghanistan, so there was a large airlift but no ground reinforcement.
Evidence suggested Politburo supervision of parts of the Soviet operation.
The greatest US risk was a quick, effective Soviet operation to pacify Afghanistan; the objective was to make it as costly as possible for the Soviets.
US covert actions authorized by the President had been very slow getting started.
The Soviets were judged to have probably passed the point of no return.
